hlni.insight: A degree label does not define assessment style; specific grading criteria do.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume B.Com and BBA have inherently different assessment styles based on their titles.
hlni.viewerChange: Viewers will now ask about specific grading criteria rather than relying on program names.
hlni.support: The method separates the work product from the assessment criteria, forcing an investigation into grading priorities.
hlni.payoff: The student learns to ask specific questions about grading, making their academic choice more informed.

candidate.reelTitle: The Assessment Audit: B.Com vs BBA
candidate.creativeAngle: Comparing degree assessment criteria rather than degree titles.
candidate.objective: Enable students to evaluate academic programs through assessment methodology.
candidate.targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Title Trap
shots.visual: Student looking at two blank notebooks labeled B.Com and BBA.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA based on names alone misses the real difference: how you are actually assessed.
shots.onscreenText: B.Com vs BBA: More than a label

shots.name: The Audit Method
shots.visual: Split-screen graphic showing a cost analysis task.
shots.dialogue: Example: Task: Analyze costs. Focus: Accuracy vs. Strategic Reasoning. Notice how the same data yields different grading priorities.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Analyze costs. Focus: Accuracy vs. Strategic Reasoning.
shots.cameraPerformance: Point of view shot of the comparison sheet.

shots.name: The Concrete Question
shots.visual: Student looking at a notepad, writing down a question.
shots.dialogue: Don't guess the focus. Ask: What specific criteria does this course use to grade my analysis? Audit the assessment, not just the title.
shots.onscreenText: What specific criteria does this course use to grade my analysis?
shots.cameraPerformance: Tight shot on the pen writing on paper.

productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic cuts synchronized with text appearance.
productionNotes.sound: Minimal ambient room tone, no music.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the student from comparing degree titles to comparing specific assessment criteria using a three-step audit method.

selected.title: The Assessment Audit
selected.audienceGap: Students assume a degree title indicates the style of assessment they will face.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Viewers learn to evaluate a course by the specific criteria of its assessments rather than the name of the degree.
selected.concept: A student compares two sample tasks side-by-side to identify that the same task can have different grading priorities.
selected.device: Split-screen comparison of a task brief versus grading rubric.
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: Two task sheets for an identical case study: one graded on accuracy, one on justification.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Analyze costs. Focus: Accuracy vs. Strategic Reasoning.
demonstration.observation: The same data set produces two different grading outcomes depending on the focus.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific criteria does this course use to grade my analysis?

comparedWith.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = assessment_questions / assessment_criteria_breakdown; Connection = task_question_journal / learning_journal_log; Discovery = insufficient_information / missing_information_audit. Each has an illustrative input, observable result and next question. This is not editorial approval.
